subject: Clarify subprocessor exportability & encryption scope for FinFlow pilot
messages:
From: Natalie G. <natalie@finflow.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finflow.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify subprocessor exportability & encryption scope for FinFlow pilot

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. As part of our procurement review ahead of the pilot, Legal/Security asked me to gather a couple of quick clarifications on Redwood's subprocessors and data export controls so we can finish the security checklist. Specifically:

- Can you share the current subprocessor roster with a note on which subprocessors have access to request/response payloads vs only telemetry/metrics?
- For any subprocessors that process data outside the EU, can you confirm whether transfers rely on SCCs, adequacy, or a customer-managed key boundary?
- Encryption: what is the default rest/in-transit encryption (algorithms), and in hosted vs private deployments how are keys managed?

If you have a short DPA reference (pdf) and the SOC 2 access link we can point the reviewers to that as well. Our timeline: we'd like these materials by end-of-week if feasible — the pilot kickoff is slated for 6/22.

Thanks,
Natalie G.
Legal Ops — FinFlow Payments
N: +1 415 555 0123

--
FinFlow is under an NDA with Redwood; please treat responses as confidential within procurement review.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie G. <natalie@finflow.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 12:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify subprocessor exportability & encryption scope for FinFlow pilot

Hi Natalie —

Appreciate the clear list. I've attached our current subprocessor roster (redwood-subprocessor-roster-20260614.csv) and the latest DPA (redwood-dpa-v3.pdf). Quick summary up front:

- Subprocessors with potential access to request/response payloads: EdgeCache Inc. (edge caching layer), TelemetryHub (metrics pipeline — only aggregated telemetry; no raw request storage by default), RealtimeLogs Ltd. (temporary log shipping — newly onboarded for CDN log delivery, see note below).
- KMS / keys: Hosted customers use Redwood-managed HSMs (CloudKeyOps) by default; for Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-kms) and can enforce key separation.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256-GCM at rest. We also perform envelope encryption for long-term storage.
- Cross-border: EdgeCache operates EU-only POPs for EU-configured deployments. TelemetryHub processes aggregated metrics in the US — transfers rely on SCCs and documented safeguards. Any customer-facing payloads remain processed within EU clusters when configured for EU residency.

Note: We recently added RealtimeLogs Ltd. as a limited-scope processor for log routing to certain CDN providers — they only receive hashed identifiers and request metadata, not plaintext user payloads. Kimberly has the exact retention and scope; I've CC'd her to add the diagram.

If you can confirm whether FinFlow needs an explicit contract addendum for this pilot (i.e., addendum that lists subprocessors and approved transfer routes), we can push a standard subprocessor addendum to DocuSign today.

Attached: redwood-subprocessor-roster-20260614.csv, redwood-dpa-v3.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Natalie G. <natalie@finflow.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify subprocessor exportability & encryption scope for FinFlow pilot

Hi — adding the technical details and a quick diagram. See attachment dataflow-redwood-finflow.svg for an annotated view of request routing and which components are in EU vs US. Key points:

- CloudKeyOps (HSM provider) maintains keys in eu-west-1 for EU-resident customers when EU residency is selected; keys are never exported. For hosted customers without EU residency selected keys are in multiregion HSMs (SCCs apply on transfers).
- RealtimeLogs Ltd. onboarding: scoped to CDN metadata only (IP, timestamp, stylized request path) — we explicitly redact bodies and PII before log shipment. Retention for these logs is 30 days, after which logs are purged.
- TelemetryHub: only aggregated metrics (no request bodies). Metrics are pseudonymized before leaving EU and transfers are covered by SCCs; we maintain a record of all transfer legal bases in our compliance repo.

SOC 2: our report is available at https://redwood.app/soc2-report/v3 (you can request a redacted copy if needed).

Action items I recommend:
1) If FinFlow requires an explicit subprocessor addendum, we'll present our standard template (I attached redwood-subprocessor-addendum-template.docx).
2) If you require KMS-in-customer-control for pilot, let us know and we'll enable the Private KMS flow (3 business days).
3) If FinFlow wants to limit RealtimeLogs for the pilot, we can turn that off within 24 hours and confirm in writing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie G. <natalie@finflow.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify subprocessor exportability & encryption scope for FinFlow pilot

Thanks Natalie — quick confirm and proposed mutual action plan (MAP):

1) Confirmation: RealtimeLogs Ltd. will not receive raw request bodies or PII for the pilot; only redacted metadata and hashed identifiers.

2) Docs we will provide today: updated subprocessor roster CSV, redwood-dpa-v3.pdf, SOC 2 link, and our standard subprocessor addendum prefilled for FinFlow (DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/sign/RWI-FINFLOW-ADDENDUM).

3) MAP / timeline (aiming to meet your 6/22 kickoff):
   - Today (6/15): Send DocuSign addendum and updated roster (ACTION: Redwood — Jonas)
   - 6/16: FinFlow counter-sign or outline required redlines (ACTION: FinFlow — Natalie / Legal)
   - 6/17–6/18: Redwood to implement any agreed flags (disable RealtimeLogs if requested, enable customer-managed KMS if requested) and confirm by email (ACTION: Redwood — Kimberly)

If that works, I'll push the addendum and you can route it to procurement/legal for signature. If you prefer, we can also route a minimal one-off rider that explicitly excludes RealtimeLogs for the pilot.

Best,
Jonas
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
